subject: Post-call: Token limits, streaming needs, and perf run next steps
messages:
From: Hugo Ramos <hugo@finova.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Aisha Malik <aisha@finova.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 12:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — latency SLOs & streaming

Kimberly, thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and a few clarifying items so we can move to a perf qualification run. 

Summary of our targets (from our end):
- P95 end-to-end generation latency: <= 350 ms for typical requests (we consider 512-token input / ~64-token streamed output as baseline).
- Peak concurrency: 200 concurrent users (wallet/account lookups) — bursts to 600 for short windows.
- Sustained TPS: ~40 req/s across our region (US) during peak hours.
- Context window: we need support for up to 8k tokens (mix of user history + document snippets). For the majority of ops 2k-4k is typical.
- Streaming: required for user visible responses (partial tokens as they are generated).

Constraints / concerns:
- We cannot accept end-user stalls beyond ~800 ms — any cold-cache behavior needs fallback.
- We have strict cost targets; if dedicated infra is required, we need clear unit-cost estimates.

Attached: finova_slo_requirements.pdf (internal SLO doc) — includes example payload shapes and a short sample of 10 representative requests.

Immediate ask: can Redwood produce an initial latency vs token-size table and a proposed perf-run matrix (date options, test harness, model variant) so we can sign off with our infra team? Also please confirm whether streaming adds measurable extra latency overhead compared with batched non-streamed responses for short outputs.

Thanks,
Hugo
Head of Product — Finova

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Hugo Ramos <hugo@finova.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — latency SLOs & streaming

Hugo — really helpful summary, appreciate you laying out the payload samples. Quick internal/next-steps recap below and a proposed test matrix attached (redwood_quick_matrix.xlsx).

What we heard / confirm:
- Baseline: 512-in / ~64-out typical; p95 <= 350 ms target; streaming required.
- Context window: up to 8k tokens, but majority 2k–4k.
- Concurrency / bursts: 200 sustained, 600 short bursts; sustained TPS ~40.

How Redwood proposes to proceed (high level):
1) Tech qualification run (2–3 days): we run controlled traffic from our Hosted environment against a candidate model variant and a Dedicated config (so you can compare). We'll deliver token-by-token latency logs, p50/p95/p99, and resource utilization.
2) Test matrix: vary input length (512, 1k, 2k, 4k, 8k), output length (32, 64, 128), and concurrency (1, 50, 200, 600). Include streaming vs non-streaming runs.
3) Deliverables: CSV of per-request latencies, a recommended config (batching, cache windows, quantization suggestion), and an ops playbook for graceful fallback (e.g., auto-downgrade to smaller model variant on sustained latency spikes).

Questions we need from you before we schedule:
- Can you confirm which 10 sample requests in the attached PDF are highest priority? (we'll use those as seed prompts for the perf harness)
- Are you okay with a one-day maintenance window if we recommend a dedicated capacity pilot?

We looped in David (solutions eng) and Marcus (perf lead) to provide the quantitative latency impact estimates and the test harness details. David — can you add a short table with estimated p95 impact by token count and by streaming vs non-streaming so Hugo has something to budget against?

Thanks — available for quick sync tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood_quick_matrix.xlsx (proposed test matrix)
From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Hugo Ramos <hugo@finova.com>, Aisha Malik <aisha@finova.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Discovery — latency SLOs & streaming

Kim / Hugo — adding the technical breakdown below. These are back-of-envelope estimates based on our recent benchmarks for similar customer profiles; final numbers will come from the qualification run but this should help with budgeting and expectations. Also attached CSV with a compact set of example numbers (performance_estimates.csv).

Quick assumptions:
- Model variant: mid-sized causal model (approx 13B), int8/quantized path available.
- Hardware: NVIDIA A10 / A100-class equivalence for Hosted tests; Dedicated options use A100x40gb or 80gb depending on model.
- Baseline tokenization: 1 token ~= 4 characters on average for English.

Estimated incremental p95 latency (tokenization + model forward + network tail):
- 512-in / 32-out (non-streaming): ~170–240 ms (p95) on hosted A100 tier with continuous batching tuned for low-latency.
- 512-in / 64-out (streaming): ~190–270 ms (p95) — streaming adds small per-token flush overhead (~10–30 ms) but reduces perceived latency for end-users since tokens arrive earlier.
- 2k-in / 64-out (streaming): ~240–380 ms (p95) — larger input increases KV cache cost and attention compute.
- 4k-in / 128-out: ~350–580 ms (p95) — this is the region where you hit more memory pressure and batching tradeoffs matter.
- 8k-in / 128-out: ~550–900 ms (p95) — may exceed your 350 ms SLO in worst-case; will need model sharding, larger instance classes, or sampling-triggered fallbacks.

Concurrency and throughput notes:
- Continuous batching reduces per-token cost but increases p95 slightly for low-latency SLOs. For strict p95 < 350 ms we recommend limiting batch window to <=8 ms and utilizing prefix caching for repeated contexts.
- For 200 concurrent users at ~40 req/s sustained, a single A100-backed Dedicated pool sized with autoscale (min 2 nodes, target 4 nodes) should be sufficient for mid-sized model variants; we'll size precisely in the run.
- Bursts to 600: enable overflow routing to a cheaper model variant (faster smaller model) as an auto-fallback for tail capacity — reduces cost and keeps responses within an acceptable latency band.

Streaming vs non-streaming:
- Streaming adds a small (10–30 ms) overhead per flush but improves perceived latency. For short outputs (<=64 tokens) streaming is a net win. For very long outputs, streaming amortizes latency and reduces buffer pressure.

Suggested perf-run parameters (what we'll run):
- Model variants: 13B quantized, 7B opt for fallback path.
- Input sizes: 512, 1k, 2k, 4k, 8k.
- Output sizes: 32, 64, 128.
- Concurrency: 1, 50, 200, 600.
- Streaming: enabled/disabled.
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 per token, CPU/GPU util, memory, KV hit rate, batch sizes.

Ops recommendations:
- Use prefix/KV caching for repeated user prompts; set a 2–5 minute cache TTL for session-level contexts.
- Use smart routing: primary route to mid-sized variant with fallback to small variant during sustained high-latency.
- If you must guarantee p95 <= 350ms at 8k contexts, Dedicated with larger GPU memory and model sharding will be required — we can show the exact delta in the run.

Next steps: if Hugo confirms sample requests and preferred run dates (we prefer Wed/Thu next week), we'll schedule the qualification and provide an initial sizing estimate within 24 hours.

-David
David Kim
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Priority sample requests: those on pages 2–3 of the attached PDF (short-auth, balance-summary, and fraud-flag explanation) — please use those as seed prompts.
- We are flexible on dates; Thu May 27 or Fri May 28 (UTC) would work for our infra folks.
- We expect to start with Hosted tests; if results show Dedicated is necessary to meet SLO/cost tradeoffs we will consider a pilot.

Can you include an estimated cost delta (hosted vs dedicated pilot) in the post-run deliverable? Also please confirm what telemetry hooks you will expose to our SREs (traces, token-level latency logs, tooling access).

Appreciate the fast turn. We'll upload an anonymized set of the 10 sample requests to the Drive link you shared later today.

Best,
Hugo
